# Good Signal Studio defaults

The consuming repository's instructions own its branch model, test commands,
dependencies, security controls and approval policy. Read those instructions
before using a shared skill. Resolve a conflict in favour of the project rule.
Do not replace or weaken an existing rule to make a shared checker pass.

Codex discovers the pinned snapshots in `.agents/skills/`. Claude Code discovers
them in `.claude/skills/`. Read the relevant `SKILL.md` and its linked references.
The installed manifest at `.github/good-signal/manifest.json` records the source
revision and file hashes. The installer does not execute the skills or their
examples. A new repository needs its own explicit enrolment.

Use the supplied PR and issue formats when the project has no format of its own.
Preserve existing templates. Publishing this bundle on GitHub does not activate
agent instructions or enforce checks in other repositories.

Capture proof on the actual revision. Report checks that were not run. Keep
secrets, private records, transcripts and personal details out of public material.
Preserve both MIT notices beside copied skills and in `.github/good-signal/`.

The bundle includes thirteen GitHub skills. Upstream examples name personal infrastructure,
accounts and templates. Use the consuming project's authorised environments,
owner and branch rules. Invoke the watcher through Python on systems where its
upstream launcher lacks execute permission. References to other drafting or review
skills are optional integrations. For drafting without them, use the project's
instructions, short factual prose, checked links and a manual diff review.
Required independent review and project verification remain blocked when the
necessary capability is missing. The builder cannot supply an independent verdict.

External messages, uploads, publication, payments, credential changes, security
control changes and destructive actions require the repository owner's approval.
`pr-body.mjs --render` sends the complete body to GitHub. Evidence attachment
uploads require their own approval. The documentation checkers' `--clone` option
executes document commands. Use it only for explicitly approved sandbox verification.

This is shared guidance. It does not grant approval, install plugins, change user
profiles or settings, provision enterprise runtimes, or configure branch protection.
